subject: design-technology
title: Smart Materials
welcome_lead: Materials that change properties when triggered.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: smart materials, SMA, photochromic, electroluminescent.
final_note: Smart materials respond to the world.

concepts.def: Shape Memory Alloy — returns to shape.

walkthroughs.body_html: Nitinol is a Shape Memory Alloy. Bend it cold, warm it up, and it snaps back to its original shape. Used in glasses frames and medical wire.
Thermochromic changes with heat — mood mugs, baby spoons that show hot food. Photochromic changes in sunlight — Transitions glasses that darken outdoors.
Electroluminescent wire glows when current passes through. Piezoelectric crystals generate voltage when pressed — used in BBQ lighters and shoe heel chargers.

mcqs.q: What does 'Rethink' mean in the 6 Rs?
options: How long the tree took to grow.
Questioning whether a product is necessary or could be designed differently for sustainability.
Trying a design again if it does not work first time.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a timber is a hardwood or softwood?
options: Whether the wood itself is physically hard or soft.
How long the tree took to grow.
The type of tree - deciduous (hardwood) or coniferous (softwood), not its hardness.

mcqs.q: What property do shape memory alloys have?
options: They remember every shape they have ever been bent into.
They return to a pre-set shape when heated.
